structural_issues: Five slugs appear twice. Each should have one owner, with a link from the other place. context-engineering (ai-agents vs ai-foundations): keep it in ai/applied. agent-evaluation (ai-agents practitioner vs ai-foundations expert): keep it in ai/agents/agentops and make the evaluation-ops version a link. amazon-cognito-user-pools-vs-identity-pools (aws-core identity vs aws-platform security-services): keep it in aws-core. secrets-management (sec-core cryptography vs sec-ops data-protection): keep it in sec-core. caching-strategies (arch-systems patterns vs eng-backend data/specialized-stores): keep the pattern in architecture and rename the data one redis-and-cache-implementation.

Topics duplicated under different slugs. Merge each cluster or give it a clear split: ai-gateway-pattern / genai-gateway-pattern / ai-gateway-security-control; model-routing-and-cascading / model-routing-and-fallback; tool-use-and-function-calling / structured-outputs-and-tool-calling; agentic-workflow-patterns / llm-workflow-patterns; sla-slo-sli-error-budgets (w2) / slis-slos-and-error-budgets (w6); chaos-engineering-resilience-testing / chaos-engineering-and-game-days; capacity-quotas-and-headroom / quotas-limits-and-capacity / capacity-planning-and-load-testing; retry-timeout-circuit-breaker-bulkhead / resilience-retries-circuit-breakers; leader-election-leases-fencing / distributed-locks-and-leases; long-running-operations-async-request-reply-durable-execution / durable-execution-workflows / durable-agent-execution; schema-evolution-and-compatibility / message-contracts-and-schema-evolution; risk-based-access-and-itdr / identity-threat-detection-and-response; physical-and-environmental-security / data-center-and-physical-security; privacy-enhancing-cryptography / privacy-enhancing-technologies; encryption-placement / encryption-at-rest-patterns; immutable-backups-ransomware-resilience / ransomware-resilience-strategy; microsoft-cloud-adoption-framework (arch-practice) / cloud-adoption-framework-for-azure (azure-core); azure-pipelines-yaml (eng-platform) / azure-pipelines-yaml-reference (azure-platform); runners-and-agents-at-scale / pipeline-agents-and-runners; github-advanced-security / configuring-ghazdo-and-defender-devops-security; five overlapping KQL and hunting articles across azure-platform, sec-ops and eng; five vector-store and vector-search articles across arch, ai, eng, azure and compare; six landing-zone and guardrail articles.

The orientation articles are triplicated. azure-ai-services-orientation (w1), foundry-tools-prebuilt-ai-services and microsoft-foundry-overview (w3) cover the same ground. So do aws-ai-services-orientation (w1), aws-ai-services-catalog and amazon-bedrock-overview (w3). Keep one orientation article per provider, tagged w1, and delete the single-article cloud/*/ai-services-overview domains.

The wave-1 exams depend on articles tagged w2 to w4. CKAD needs kubernetes-architecture (w4) and kubernetes-monitoring-and-logging (w6). AI-901 and AIF-C01 need llm-api-fundamentals, prompt-engineering, rag-end-to-end, customization-decision-framework, genai-evaluation-fundamentals, microsoft-foundry-overview, foundry-quickstart-chat-and-agent-clients, amazon-bedrock-overview, sagemaker-ai-for-genai, agentic-ai-fundamentals and ai-threat-landscape, all tagged w3. SC-900 needs entra-id-tenants (w2) plus microsoft-purview-orientation, microsoft-sentinel, microsoft-defender-xdr, authentication-factors-and-mfa and sso-and-federation (all w4). CLF-C02 needs every aws-core foundation article (w2), aws-security-services-map (w4) and estimating-and-guarding-aws-spend (w2). Three w1 labs (first GenAI app, prebuilt AI services, security first look) have no w1 articles behind them.

The wave-2 exams also depend on later waves. AI-200 4.1 needs azure-key-vault-in-practice (w4). SAA-C03:D1 needs aws-kms-in-depth, secrets-manager-vs-parameter-store and certificates-acm-and-private-ca (all w4). AI-200 2.1.2 needs consistency-models (w5). SAA-C03:D2 needs event-driven-architecture, caching-strategies, serverless-architecture and stateless-vs-stateful-services (all w5). AI-200 3.1.1 needs retries-and-dead-letter-queues and delivery-semantics (w5).

Concepts are scheduled after the products that use them. The vendor-neutral sec-core IAM and cryptography sets (OAuth, OIDC, JWT, envelope encryption, TLS) are w4, two waves after Entra app registrations, consent and KMS (w2). eng-backend messaging and data are w5, after Service Bus, SQS, Cosmos DB and DynamoDB (w2). devops iac, ci-cd, observability and sre are w6, after the w2 OpenTelemetry lab, azure-pipelines and pipeline OIDC articles, and IaC used from w1. iac-fundamentals as a foundation article in w6 is the clearest case.

Some level and wave tags contradict each other. cluster-lifecycle-upgrades-and-etcd is w1 but serves CKA (w4). admission-control-and-policy-engines is expert at w1, although CKAD needs only 'understand admission control'; split it into a w1 foundation article and a w4 Kyverno/VAP/Gatekeeper article. kubernetes-architecture is a foundation article but tagged w4. agent-evaluation is practitioner in one section and expert in the other.

The waves are badly unbalanced: w1 has 69 articles for five exams, w2 has 353, w3 171, w4 179, w5 145 and w6 58. Wave 2 is too big to finish as one unit. Split it into 2a (AZ-104 and SAA-C03 infrastructure) and 2b (AI-200 app platform and data), and move the foundation-level aws-core and azure-core articles into w1.

Several articles sit in the wrong place. The vendor-neutral cloud/foundations domain belongs to the azure-core section; move it to compare or treat it as neutral. Language and runtime articles (dotnet-csharp, python-for-csharp-engineers, aspnet-core-vs-fastapi, async-threading) and the whole apis domain sit under messaging/, which hurts navigation. Accept it and document it as 'messaging = backend services', or ask for a backend area. ai/evaluation-ops (25 articles) mixes classic MLOps, GenAIOps and platform concerns; move the gateway, routing and caching articles to ai/platforms.

Several provider articles lack a counterpart. AWS has none for azure-migrate-for-servers, azure-batch-and-hpc-options, azure-app-configuration-and-feature-flags (AWS AppConfig is named in AIP-C01 1.2.2) or Azure Arc (Systems Manager hybrid nodes). Azure has none for hosting-angular-on-aws, terraform-on-aws or sagemaker-ai-for-genai (Azure Machine Learning). Each of these breaks the 'map to the other provider' promise.

Two slugs are tied to versions that will date soon. stack-upgrade-dotnet10-angular22 will age in November 2026, when .NET 11 and Angular 23 are expected. mcp-2026-07-28-what-changed has the same problem. Use stable slugs such as dotnet-and-angular-upgrade-playbook and mcp-spec-changes, with dated sections inside.

The compare section has only 14 glossary terms for about 61 compare articles. The Rosetta and fidelity-rating promise needs paired, rated terms, such as 'Private Endpoint ~ interface VPC endpoint (high fidelity)', in the glossary so that compare pages can cross-link them.

The practice layer has wave mismatches. The Key Vault vs KMS lab is w4, but AI-200 and SAA-C03 need it in w2. No lab exercises IaC before w6. No lab covers AZ-104 identity, App Service or backup. Capstone B (w3) relies on the threat-model and AI-security articles, so schedule it after them.
sequencing_advice:
Step 0, before writing anything: resolve the 5 duplicate slugs and the duplicate clusters, merge the triplicated AI orientation articles, and re-tag the waves. Then write by exam slice. Within each wave the order is: vendor-neutral concept, then the Azure article, then the AWS article, then the cloud-compare article, then the lab, cheatsheet or reference. Keep 'rosetta' as a living skeleton from day one and add a row each time a compare article ships. Track coverage with exam refs (e.g. CKAD:D2), and call a wave exam-ready only when every objective of its exams maps to a finished article.
Wave 1, grown from 69 to about 130 articles: cloud/foundations; the foundation-level aws-core and azure-core articles (IAM, EC2, VPC, global infrastructure, Entra tenants, resource organization, cost); sec-core foundations plus authentication-vs-authorization, authentication-factors-and-mfa, sso-and-federation and cryptography-fundamentals; Microsoft security orientation (Purview, Sentinel, Defender XDR) and the new trust-portal and support compare articles; ai-foundations plus the foundation-level ai/applied, Foundry and Bedrock orientation and quickstart articles, agentic-ai-fundamentals and ai-threat-landscape; the full CKAD set, including kubernetes-architecture, monitoring and logging, deprecations, native canary and the Linux primer; docker, oci, iac-fundamentals, hosting-angular on both clouds.
Wave 2a (AZ-104, SAA-C03 infrastructure): identity, governance, networking, compute, storage, monitoring, backup and DR, the reliability set, plus the vendor-neutral prerequisites pulled forward: OAuth, OIDC, JWT, key-management and envelope encryption, secrets-management, the merged SLO article, observability-fundamentals and opentelemetry-in-practice, and the Terraform language basics. Wave 2b (AI-200, app platform): containers, serverless, messaging, data, the practitioner Key Vault, KMS, Secrets Manager and ACM articles (moved from w4), delivery-semantics, retries-and-DLQ, idempotency, outbox, consistency-models, caching, NoSQL modelling, basic vector search, Aspire, OpenAPI, and the CDK and Bicep IaC lab.
Wave 3: practitioner ai/applied, then protocols (MCP before the MCP-hosting and gateway articles), then platforms, then ai-security, then agentops. Write the labs in this order: RAG, then MCP server, then secure MCP, then agent, then multi-agent, then agent CI/CD. Capstone B comes last, after the MCP and RAG threat models.
Wave 4: sec-core IAM, crypto and appsec depth; sec-ops cloud security, detection and network; the AWS and Azure security services, including the new centralized logging and edge security articles; then CKA, then CKS, with kubeadm, CRI/CSI/CNI and CoreDNS before the CKA labs. Tabletops come after the IR articles, and Capstone C closes the wave.
Wave 5: arch-practice, then arch-systems patterns and distributed systems (whatever was not pulled forward), migration and FinOps, the Well-Architected AI article, the katas and Capstone A.
Wave 6: GRC (including BCM, assessment and testing, and personnel), TOGAF, CPSA-F refinements, the AIGP set (impact assessments), the TA-004 extras (Vault, import and refactoring, HCP Terraform, OpenTofu), then Capstone D.
Within each wave, write the hub article (the 'choosing' guide or decision guide) of each domain first, so that later articles have something to link to.
summary:
The blueprint is broad (975 planned articles) and covers most objectives in the wave exams. The main problems are sequencing and duplication rather than missing breadth. The biggest issue is wave tagging. The five wave-1 exams (CKAD, AI-901, SC-900, CLF-C02, AIF-C01) depend on articles tagged w2 to w4 (kubernetes-architecture, the Foundry and Bedrock orientations, prompt engineering, RAG, Entra, Purview, Sentinel, the aws-core foundations). Wave 2 (353 articles) depends on Key Vault, KMS, consistency and messaging concepts scheduled in w4 and w5. Throughout, vendor-neutral concepts (IAM, crypto, messaging, IaC, CI/CD, observability) are scheduled after the products that use them. The plan has 5 exact duplicate slugs (context-engineering, agent-evaluation, amazon-cognito-user-pools-vs-identity-pools, secrets-management, caching-strategies) and about 20 near-duplicate clusters, the largest being AI gateway and routing, SLOs, chaos engineering, CAF, Azure Pipelines, KQL hunting and vector search.

Concrete content gaps:
- **IaC and Kubernetes:** AWS CDK in C# and Python; Terraform Vault, import and refactoring, and testing (TA-004); kubeadm and HA, CRI/CSI/CNI, CoreDNS, API deprecations, Kubernetes-native canary and a Linux primer (CKA, CKAD, CKS).
- **AWS counterparts:** migration services, Elastic Disaster Recovery and ARC, Batch/HPC/EMR, centralized security logging with Security Lake, and edge security with WAF, Shield Advanced and Firewall Manager.
- **Compare articles:** Purview vs Macie, data catalogs, data perimeters, chaos and load testing, support plans and marketplaces, trust portals, and MCRA/MCSB vs AWS SRA.
- **AI:** MCP hosting on Functions, APIM and Lambda; deployment types and capacity (PTU, cross-Region inference); Hugging Face and open models; agent developer tooling; Q Developer and Kiro vs Copilot; AI impact assessments (AIGP).
- **Security:** BCM and BIA; a security assessment and testing programme; personnel, ethics and investigations; network protocols and wireless (CISSP); endpoint, mobile and Intune; Microsoft 365 security; AD DS hardening with the enterprise access model and PAW (SC-100).
- **Architecture and engineering:** Well-Architected for AI; OpenAPI and GraphQL; Aspire; agent UI in Angular; micro-frontends; Static Web Apps.
- **Practice:** labs for Bicep and CDK (w2), backup and ASR, a cross-cloud BGP VPN, AZ-104 identity and App Service, and agent CI/CD, plus a data-platform kata.

The fix is to resolve the duplicates and re-tag the waves first, grow w1 and split w2 into 2a and 2b, and then write concept, Azure, AWS, compare and lab in that order within each wave.
